body:
Oxide Computer Company has raised $445 million in Series D financing led by Eclipse, providing capital to expand manufacturing capacity as demand grows for its on-premises cloud infrastructure systems.

The funding round included existing investors US Innovative Technology Fund, Riot Ventures and Jane Street, along with new investors Atreides Management and AMD Ventures.

The Emeryville, California-based company said it reached profitability earlier in 2026 and has increased manufacturing capacity twentyfold over the past 12 months. Despite that expansion, customer demand continues to exceed production capacity.

“The accelerating pace of on-prem cloud computing projects has required us to scale manufacturing capacity by 20x over the past 12 months, and yet demand still exceeds supply,” said **Steve Tuck**, co-founder and CEO of Oxide. “This funding will allow us to aggressively invest in the materials and manufacturing scale our customers need for years to come.”

Oxide develops the Cloud Computer, a rack-scale system that combines purpose-built hardware with open-source software to provide cloud computing capabilities within customer-owned data centers. The platform integrates compute, storage, networking and management software into a unified infrastructure system.

The company is positioning its technology as an alternative for enterprises seeking cloud-style automation while retaining direct control over infrastructure, data security, performance and operating costs.

Oxide said growing demand for AI infrastructure, particularly workloads involving autonomous AI agents, is increasing requirements for computing capacity, memory and networking. Its customers include organizations in financial services, government, national laboratories and aerospace.

AMD Ventures’ participation expands an existing technical relationship between AMD and Oxide, which have collaborated across hardware and software development.

“Oxide’s systems-level approach to enterprise infrastructure is expanding the choices available to customers as their computing needs become more complex,” said **Sagi Paz**, head of AMD Ventures.

The new capital will primarily support component procurement, manufacturing expansion and fulfillment of existing and future customer orders.

Founded in 2019, Oxide Computer Company develops integrated hardware and open-source software systems designed to bring hyperscale-style cloud infrastructure capabilities to enterprise-owned data centers.
